tldr: Page 74 captures survey responses from Oregon residents and business representatives on economic competitiveness. Dominant themes: excessive tax and regulatory burden deter business formation; small businesses (82% of economy) need support; K-12 education ranked 41st-47th requires increased investment; Climate Protection Program threatens energy jobs and affordability; construction workforce shortage; agricultural land loss accelerating (120K-140K acres/year); rural communities neglected. Respondents advocate: consolidate state portals, streamline permitting, reform taxes (add sales tax, reduce income tax), protect farmland, enact worker-centered energy policy.

bullets.text: Small businesses represent 82% of Oregon's economy but face disproportionate regulatory burden; respondents cite need to consolidate multiple state websites into single portal with one login
K-12 education ranking 41st-47th nationally; respondents call for legislative priority and investment, with one noting ranking improves to 24th when funding increases

Climate Protection Program identified as highest carbon pricing in North America; union workers and energy employees cite $4.9 Billion cost to natural gas consumers over 2025-2035 period and threat to family-wage jobs
Healthcare costs barrier for small businesses; respondents demand parity with large employers or regulation preventing tiered health plan offerings
Oregon losing 120,000-140,000 acres agricultural land annually; landowners call for rezoning protections and equal voice in land-use decisions alongside data centers and solar/wind development
Construction workforce shortage: apprentice-to-journeyman ratio needs increase from 1:1 to 1:2 to accelerate training capacity
January 2026 QSBS tax policy change (revocation) called devastating to startup ecosystem; Oregon only state taking 10% of startup sale earnings

Untapped talent pool (people with disabilities, reentry workers, justice-involved individuals) identified; respondents propose hiring incentives and recognition programs modeled on Missouri Inclusion Award
Rural communities feel neglected by Salem; respondents propose rural-oriented Prosperity Council offshoot to address local workforce retention and economic development
Tax structure disparity: 48 states have sales taxes; respondents call for Oregon to implement sales tax and reduce income tax to improve competitiveness and capture tourism revenue

bureaus: Department of Consumer and Business Services
